newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Japan says Sri Lankan war deters investors.
newsitem.headline: Japan says Sri Lankan war deters investors.

text.p: Japanese companies are holding back from investing in Sri Lanka because of the island's 13-year-old ethnic war, a top Japanese industry official said on Saturday.

"Sri Lanka will have to resolve the ethnic crisis as soon as possible and improve the infrastructure," Shigeo Hashimoto, executive-director of the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry told a news conference after a meeting of the Japan-Sri Lanka Business Cooperation Committee.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels are battling government troops for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
"Security is the top worry. People don't like to go where there are security problems," Hashimoto later told Reuters.
Hashimoto said Sri Lanka's 19 million population was too small a domestic market to attract large investments.
He said things might change once the proposed South Asian Preferential Trade Agreement (SAPTA) came into force. The agreement is meant to ease trade barriers among seven countries in the region.
Japan's is Sri Lanka's largest aid donor. Its exports to Sri Lanka amounted to $400 million in 1996 and imports were $280 million, Japanese officials said.
